mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increase and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increase and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of periods with declining GDP, or the correlation between GDP decline and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production index by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increase and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.5% in a month, the combined effect of high interest rates and inflationary pressure typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: high inflation and tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 300,000 in a month and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.3%, the combined effect of strong job growth and falling unemployment typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending improve.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 300,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease on positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts by more than 10% in a month signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the housing market is a leading indicator of broader economic demand.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between HOUST decline and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased consumer spending supports corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of periods with increasing RSAFS, or the correlation between RSAFS increase and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
